concerns.text: Task T010 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it produces `code/requirements.txt`, which is a required input for many downstream tasks (e.g., T001, T003). Running T010 in parallel with any consumer could cause a race condition, so the `[P]` tag is unsafe.

Task T011 is marked `[P]` yet it creates `code/R/renv.lock`, a file later needed by the modeling scripts. Parallel execution with consumers would break reproducibility, making the `[P]` designation incorrect.

Task T000 is marked `[P]` but it executes a minimal end‑to‑end pipeline that writes result artifacts (`merged_analysis_sample.csv`, `model_summary_sample.csv`, etc.). These files are also written by later full‑pipeline tasks, so parallel runs could overwrite each other; the task is not parallel‑safe.

Task T012 is marked `[P]` yet it updates the global state hash file after each pipeline step. If executed concurrently with any other task that also writes to the state YAML, the updates would conflict, violating parallel safety.
